channel.title: Kseniia's Good News
channel.description: Positive news from several sources, scored 0-10 for goodness and refreshed every six hours.

item.title: India releases two captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the wild [7/10]
item.description: Two captive-bred male Great Indian Bustards were released into Desert National Park in Rajasthan as an experiment to rebuild the critically endangered species. (Goodness 7/10: Hopeful step for a critically endangered bird; outcome uncertain.)

item.title: Purple bacteria powder matched synthetic fertilizer in crop trials [6/10]
item.description: Dried powder from the purple bacterium Rhodovulum sulfidophilum matched synthetic fertilizers in a two-year trial, hinting at a lower-impact option. (Goodness 6/10: Promising alternative, but early-stage.)

item.title: South African jurist Navi Pillay wins the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize [7/10]
item.description: The Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Peace Prize to Navi Pillay, a South African judge, for her work promoting peace and international justice. (Goodness 7/10: Major recognition for human rights work.)

item.title: A teenager's project redirects surplus hospital supplies abroad [7/10]
item.description: Project MedBridge, started by 16-year-old Ben Kurian, sends surplus medical supplies from Ohio hospitals to places that need them, rescuing millions of dollars of items. (Goodness 7/10: Practical waste-to-aid model with measurable results.)

item.title: New species of egg-eating snake found in Ethiopian highlands [6/10]
item.description: A new nonvenomous egg-eating snake, the white-throated egg-eater, has been documented in Ethiopia's Harenna Forest. (Goodness 6/10: A new species adds to knowledge and the case for protecting the forest.)

item.title: Goan mother grows ten jars of home recipes into a global business [6/10]
item.description: A woman in Goa who began with ten jars in 2010 now sells traditional Goan masalas and pickles to customers around the world. (Goodness 6/10: A good small-business story for one family and local food traditions.)

item.title: Chennai engineer uses information requests to protect elephants and a lake [7/10]
item.description: A civil engineer in Chennai has used Right to Information requests to expose elephant deaths on rail tracks and help clean a lake, and now explains how others can do the same. (Goodness 7/10: Shows ordinary citizens can drive accountability, though results are local.)

item.title: Floating scarecrow cuts seabird deaths in fishing nets by up to 71 percent [8/10]
item.description: A bird-shaped kite and a spinning, eyed buoy reduced seabird bycatch in Cornish gillnets by up to 71 percent in trials. (Goodness 8/10: Cheap, effective tool that could spread to other fisheries.)

item.title: Jonathan the tortoise, about 194, contributes first epigenome to aging research [6/10]
item.description: Researchers ran genetic tests on Jonathan, an estimated 194-year-old giant tortoise, to learn about aging; it is the first epigenome from such a long-lived animal. (Goodness 6/10: Interesting aging research from a single animal; benefits are still distant.)

item.title: Interpol operation in Latin America leads to hundreds of arrests [7/10]
item.description: Interpol's Operation Madre Tierra across nine countries led to hundreds of arrests and the recovery of over 1,000 animals from wildlife and timber trafficking. (Goodness 7/10: Meaningful enforcement success, though trafficking persists.)

item.title: Australia's new environmental agency busts wildlife trafficking ring [6/10]
item.description: Australia's National Environmental Protection Agency seized 28 native animals and about A$300,000 in alleged trafficking proceeds in a major operation. (Goodness 6/10: Shows new enforcement capacity working.)

item.title: A strange yellow coral off Costa Rica forms a new evolutionary lineage [6/10]
item.description: Scientists found a yellow coral off Costa Rica that fits no known family, so they created a new one for it, adding to knowledge of deep-sea life. (Goodness 6/10: New knowledge about marine biodiversity.)

item.title: Homo erectus fossils in South Africa are 200,000 years older than expected [6/10]
item.description: Fossils from Drimolen Cave, including a skull fragment dated to about 2 million years, push back the known age of Homo erectus. (Goodness 6/10: Notable scientific discovery with no direct practical benefit.)

item.title: Delhi tutor's free classes grow into a movement that cleaned 250 public spaces [7/10]
item.description: Vinay Das began free classes for migrant children in Wazirpur; weekend clean-up drives since 2018 have cleared around 250 parks and streets. (Goodness 7/10: Community-led effort helping children and neighborhoods.)

item.title: Solar grows as an alternative to Nigeria's unreliable grid [6/10]
item.description: Nigeria's power crisis is creating opportunities for solar energy, according to a Business Africa segment. (Goodness 6/10: Clean energy growth, though scale and benefit are unclear.)

item.title: Free kit helps UK communities prepare for emergencies [6/10]
item.description: Prince William launched a free how-to resource that helps local communities build resilience and prepare for emergencies. (Goodness 6/10: A practical, free tool for community preparedness.)

item.title: Twenty kidnapped Nigerian graduates found alive after week-long search [6/10]
item.description: Graduates abducted while travelling to begin national youth service were rescued, authorities confirmed. (Goodness 6/10: Safe return for 20 people, though the kidnapping itself was harmful.)

item.title: More than 14,000 explosives cleared from a Libyan city and nearby farmland [7/10]
item.description: Demining teams backed by the UN and others cleared over 14,000 leftover explosives this year, making homes and farmland safer in a coastal Libyan city. (Goodness 7/10: Real safety gain for a community, though much clearance remains.)

item.title: New York students help improve school lunch by surveying classmates [7/10]
item.description: Through Youth Food Advocates, a Brooklyn student surveyed classmates on why they skipped the cafeteria and what they wanted to eat. (Goodness 7/10: Student-led change that can improve meals for many pupils.)

item.title: Bengaluru's Hesaraghatta grassland becomes a conservation reserve [8/10]
item.description: After nearly two decades of campaigning, Karnataka notified about 5,678 acres of Hesaraghatta grassland as a conservation reserve. (Goodness 8/10: Lasting habitat protection won by citizens near a big city.)

item.title: Berlin volunteers water 900,000 mapped street trees [7/10]
item.description: Berlin's Giess den Kiez app maps about 900,000 street trees and lets 12,000 volunteers coordinate with city crews to water them during heat waves. (Goodness 7/10: A working community model that helps city trees survive heat, though local in scale.)

item.title: London's Oxford Street to close to vehicles this month [6/10]
item.description: Oxford Street will close to all vehicles between Orchard Street and Great Portland Street this month, creating a large pedestrian zone in central London. (Goodness 6/10: Cleaner, safer public space for many people, with effects still to be seen.)

item.title: Stanford molecule turns a cancer driver protein into a self-destruct trigger [6/10]
item.description: Stanford scientists designed a molecule that repurposes a lymphoma-promoting protein to activate cell-death pathways. In mice it eliminated aggressive tumors. (Goodness 6/10: Promising but only shown in mice so far.)

item.title: Satellite tags reveal long journeys of Olive Ridley turtles off Odisha [6/10]
item.description: A three-year Wildlife Institute of India study tracks Olive Ridley turtles with satellite tags and boat surveys. One turtle was followed for 6,719 km. (Goodness 6/10: New data can improve turtle protection.)

item.title: Odisha woman teaches herself tyre repair to support her family [6/10]
item.description: After her husband was injured, Suni Hembram taught herself tyre repair and now runs a roadside repair shop, lifting heavy tyres herself. (Goodness 6/10: Inspiring for one family and community.)

item.title: Profile of Dr Si Padmavati, India's first woman cardiologist [6/10]
item.description: The story covers her work treating underprivileged heart patients, which she continued for long hours into her mid-nineties. (Goodness 6/10: A tribute to lasting service to patients.)

item.title: Raipur family turns forest seeds into chocolate and cosmetic ingredients [6/10]
item.description: A family business in Raipur has grown to about Rs 1,357 crore by processing forest seeds into ingredients for chocolate and cosmetics. (Goodness 6/10: A local enterprise making use of overlooked natural materials.)

item.title: Study maps habitat of the little-known Mishmi takin in Arunachal Pradesh [6/10]
item.description: Researchers combined Indigenous knowledge with camera-trap surveys to map the seasonal movements and habitat use of the Mishmi takin in the Dibang Valley. (Goodness 6/10: Useful conservation knowledge built with local communities.)

item.title: Strangers repair storm-damaged Kansas home after TV appeal [6/10]
item.description: A Kansas man whose house was hit by a fallen tree asked for a tarp on local TV. Neighbours and strangers who saw it came to cover the roof. (Goodness 6/10: Small-scale community kindness, limited reach.)

item.title: Threatened sand gazelles breed at a Saudi solar park [7/10]
item.description: A solar plant near the Red Sea coast, inside a nature reserve in Saudi Arabia, is hosting breeding Arabian sand gazelles, a vulnerable species. (Goodness 7/10: Renewable energy coexisting with wildlife recovery, though local in scale.)

item.title: Africa launches its own credit rating agency [6/10]
item.description: A new African credit rating agency aims to offer assessments seen as fairer, with the goal of lowering borrowing costs for African governments. (Goodness 6/10: Could cut borrowing costs, but results are yet to be seen.)

item.title: Kagan and Soai win Nobel Prize in chemistry [6/10]
item.description: Henri Kagan of France and Kenso Soai of Japan won the chemistry prize for explaining the chemical origin of life's asymmetry. (Goodness 6/10: Recognition of fundamental science with long-term value.)

item.title: Father walks again three years after a serious brain injury [6/10]
item.description: A father who spent three years recovering from a car-accident brain injury surprised his children by walking unaided again. (Goodness 6/10: A moving recovery, but it concerns one family.)

item.title: California allows plug-in balcony solar panels [7/10]
item.description: A new California law lets residents install small solar arrays on balconies and plug them into standard outlets. Other states may follow. (Goodness 7/10: Practical clean-energy access for renters and apartment dwellers, though still a single-state step.)

item.title: Nearly 1,000 Delhi students clear 2,000 kg of waste from the Yamuna [6/10]
item.description: On Gandhi Jayanti, about 1,000 Delhi University students collected more than 2,000 kilograms of waste along the Yamuna River. (Goodness 6/10: Strong community action, though a one-day effort.)

item.title: Tiny Myristica swamp forests in the Western Ghats shelter wildlife and water [6/10]
item.description: These rare freshwater forests, smaller than a playground, hold water, feed streams and support over 200 butterfly species. (Goodness 6/10: Highlights valuable habitat worth protecting.)

item.title: Mumbai volunteers turn 18,000 kg of beach plastic into school benches [7/10]
item.description: More than 1,500 volunteers collected 18,000 kg of plastic in a beach cleanup; it will be recycled into benches for students across Maharashtra. (Goodness 7/10: Cleans coasts and helps schools.)

item.title: Morocco appoints its first woman prime minister [7/10]
item.description: King Mohammed VI named Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, a former Marrakesh mayor and urban planner, as head of government, a first for the country. (Goodness 7/10: A milestone for women's representation, though its practical effect on policy is yet to be seen.)

item.title: Drug target could ease brain inflammation tied to Alzheimer's and Parkinson's [6/10]
item.description: Blocking the P2X7 receptor strongly reduced inflammation in human brain tissue. The result may allow existing drugs to be repurposed for these diseases. (Goodness 6/10: Early tissue-level result, but with a route to repurposed drugs.)

item.title: Feeding zoo lions whole carcasses brings out more natural behavior [6/10]
item.description: Zoo lions fed whole carcasses on a feast-and-fast schedule spent about three times longer eating and showed more natural activity rhythms. (Goodness 6/10: A simple welfare improvement for captive animals.)

item.title: International Whaling Commission rejects push to revive commercial whaling [8/10]
item.description: A proposal to open a path back to commercial whaling was withdrawn at the commission's meeting in Hobart, leaving the 1986 moratorium in place. (Goodness 8/10: Protects whales from a return to commercial hunting.)

item.title: Donors exceed pledge to fund Indigenous and local forest land rights [6/10]
item.description: Donors delivered about $2.35 billion from 2021 to 2025, above a $1.7 billion pledge. Only a small share goes directly to community organizations. (Goodness 6/10: Target beaten, but direct funding remains low.)

item.title: Thai rescue centre prepares orphaned leopard cats for release [6/10]
item.description: A wildlife centre in northeastern Thailand rehabilitates orphaned leopard cats, teaching them behaviors needed to survive before returning them to the wild. (Goodness 6/10: Rescue and release work, limited in scale.)

item.title: Southern right whales return to South African town of Hermanus [7/10]
item.description: Hundreds of southern right whales migrate from Antarctica each year, drawing visitors to Hermanus between June and November. (Goodness 7/10: Healthy whale presence and local joy.)

item.title: Nokia and NASA plan 4G network for the Moon [6/10]
item.description: NASA is working with Nokia's Bell Labs to set up 4G mobile connectivity on the Moon, aiming to improve astronaut communication and cut operating costs. (Goodness 6/10: Useful space technology, but still a plan.)

item.title: Kargil teacher turns old war bunkers into history classrooms [7/10]
item.description: An educator in Kargil has converted abandoned military bunkers into interactive classrooms where children learn the region's history by experiencing it first-hand. (Goodness 7/10: Creative local education initiative that benefits a community, though limited in reach.)

item.title: Morocco's Salé festival celebrates women filmmakers [6/10]
item.description: After 22 years, the festival continues to examine opportunities, funding and roles for women in cinema. (Goodness 6/10: Supports women in film.)

item.title: Illinois residents honored for rescuing driver from flooded pond [6/10]
item.description: Local residents and police officers worked together to rescue an elderly driver whose vehicle plunged into a flooded retention pond during a storm. (Goodness 6/10: A life saved, a local act of courage.)

item.title: Chess grows popular among prisoners in Kenya [6/10]
item.description: Prisoners are taking up chess as a rehabilitation activity, with participants reporting less impulsive behavior. (Goodness 6/10: Small but real rehabilitation benefit.)

item.title: Couples who exercise together report stronger relationships [6/10]
item.description: A study found couples who work out together report better communication, conflict resolution and lower marital stress than those who exercise alone. Even walking together may help. (Goodness 6/10: A simple, accessible habit linked to wellbeing, though the findings are correlational.)

item.title: Off-grid solar helps Amazon communities replace diesel [8/10]
item.description: More than 100,000 off-grid solar systems now supply clean water and power to remote Indigenous and riverside communities in the Brazilian Amazon, helping them prepare for drought. (Goodness 8/10: Large real-world rollout that cuts fuel use and improves resilience.)

item.title: Kelp restoration off British Columbia combines science and Indigenous knowledge [7/10]
item.description: A collaborative project has planted over 4,200 square meters of new kelp habitat off Canada's Pacific coast, with sea otters also helping the ecosystem recover. (Goodness 7/10: Concrete habitat gain, though still modest in scale.)

item.title: Artificial nests help Hong Kong's endangered cockatoos [6/10]
item.description: Conservationists are installing nest boxes for critically endangered yellow-crested cockatoos in Hong Kong, giving them homes and a way to study their behavior. (Goodness 6/10: Practical help for a critically endangered species.)

item.title: Solar farms in China's Gobi Desert reduce dust storms [7/10]
item.description: Solar installations in the Gobi Desert cut dust emissions by over 352,000 metric tons a month by roughening terrain and stabilizing soil. (Goodness 7/10: A useful extra benefit of clean energy.)

item.title: Virginia enacts Clean Slate law for minor offenses [7/10]
item.description: Virginia's new law automatically seals misdemeanor records, helping residents get jobs and financial opportunities without past convictions holding them back. (Goodness 7/10: Helps many people rebuild their lives.)

item.title: Bihar village school teaches 660 students with offline digital lessons [7/10]
item.description: A government secondary school in Sarai Tand, Bihar, uses a smart classroom with offline digital content, so 660 students across grades can learn without needing internet access. (Goodness 7/10: Low-cost technology widens access to learning for hundreds of rural pupils.)

item.title: 92-year-old Gujarat grandmother starts crochet business with granddaughters [6/10]
item.description: A 92-year-old woman in Gujarat has turned her lifelong love of crochet into a handmade business, run together with her granddaughters. (Goodness 6/10: A heartening story for one family and a model of working later in life.)

item.title: Gurugram startup offers women-only rides with female drivers [7/10]
item.description: Fery Rides, founded by three people in Gurugram, runs electric vehicles driven by women for women passengers, with no surge pricing, responding to safety concerns on commutes. (Goodness 7/10: Safer, cleaner transport for women, though still a small local service.)

item.title: Volunteers help 100,000 amphibians cross roads in New Hampshire [7/10]
item.description: New Hampshire's Salamander Brigades, volunteer groups that help salamanders and frogs cross roads during their yearly migration, have now assisted around 100,000 animals. (Goodness 7/10: Community action is directly protecting amphibian populations.)

item.title: Boston plans battery-powered commuter trains on Fairmount Line [6/10]
item.description: Boston's transit authority intends to run battery trains on the Fairmount Line by 2030, testing electrification without overhead wires and aiming for more frequent, cleaner service. (Goodness 6/10: Cleaner transit, but not before 2030.)
